candidates.statement: One says that an indecomposable multi-fusion category C′ is a quotient category of an indecomposable multi-fusion category C if there exists a tensor functor F : C →C′ such that any object of C′ is a subobject of F(X), X ∈C (See Section 5). It follows from the above that a given multi-fusion category C has only ﬁnitely many quotient categories.

A module category M over a multi-fusion category C does not admit nontrivial deformations. In particular, the number of such module categories (up to equivalence) with a given number of simple objects is ﬁnite. To prove Corollary 2.35, it suﬃces to choose a semisimple algebra R with number of blocks equal to the number of simple objects in M, and apply Theorem 2.31 to the functor F : C →R −bimod associated with M.

candidates.statement: Let G be a ﬁnite group, and C = VecG be the category of G-graded vector spaces over an algebraically closed ﬁeld k (of any characteristic). Then Hi(C) = Hi(O(G)), the Hochschild cohomology of O(G) as a coalgebra, where O(G) is the Hopf algebra of k-valued functions on G. In other words, Hi(C) = Hi(G, k), the group cohomology of G with coeﬃcients in k.
